one_liner: Header-only C++11 SWAR-accelerated string_view alternative; faster find/rfind/find_first_of than std::string_view, slower on not_of scans.
what_it_does: zuu_string_view is a non-owning, zero-copy view type that brings std::string_view-style ergonomics (find, rfind, find_first_of/last_of, find_first_not_of/last_not_of, substr) to C++11 codebases that can't move to C++17. It's templated over char, wchar_t, char8_t/16_t/32_t, is constructible from C strings, char arrays, std::string, and (when compiled as C++17+) std::string_view, and converts implicitly back to std::string and std::string_view. It is not a strict drop-in: size_type/npos is `unsigned int` (32-bit), not std::size_t, so return values and npos comparisons differ from std::string_view's.
how_it_is_fast: The positive-search functions (find, rfind, find_first_of, find_last_of) use SWAR (SIMD-within-a-register): they memcpy 8 bytes at a time into a uint64_t 'tape', broadcast the needle byte(s) across all 8 lanes, XOR against the tape, and apply the classic branchless haszero/hasless byte-detection trick (0x7F7F...7F and 0x8080...80 masks) plus count_trailing_zeros/count_leading_zeros to locate the matching byte in one shot instead of a per-byte loop. Multi-char searches (find_first_of family) extend this with a 256-bit bitmap built from 4 uint64_t lookup words. This path only triggers for sizeof(CharT)==1 outside constexpr evaluation; everything else falls back to a scalar loop.
when_to_use: Hot-path find/rfind/find_first_of/find_last_of/find(char) calls over ASCII/byte strings (README's own test string is ~95 chars) where a few nanoseconds per call matters
C++11-only codebases that want string_view-style ergonomics without raising the language standard
Header-only vendoring is acceptable: just include/zuu/string_view.hpp + include/zuu/char_class.hpp, no build step
Single-threaded or read-only-shared usage (it's a raw pointer+length pair with no internal synchronization)
Data provably under ~4 billion characters, since length is stored as a 32-bit unsigned int
when_not_to_use: find_first_not_of / find_last_not_of-heavy code: the README's own numbers show zuu 20-26% slower than std::string_view there
Buffers that could exceed ~4B characters, or code that assumes std::string_view's std::size_t-typed npos/return values

wchar_t/char16_t/char32_t workloads or constexpr contexts: the SWAR path is disabled there (sizeof(CharT)==1 and non-constexpr only), so performance likely reduces to the scalar fallback, which is unbenchmarked
Projects that need a licensed dependency to ship: no LICENSE file and no license field in vcpkg.json
Teams wanting proven maturity: repo created 2026-09-11, all 30 commits land within about a day, 0 stars, 0 issues, no third-party validation

integration.dependencies: none for the library itself (Google Benchmark and GoogleTest are dev-only, pulled via vcpkg for building the tests/benchmarks)
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (CI builds it under GCC, Clang, MSVC, and Apple Clang with -DCMAKE_CXX_STANDARD=11); CMake 3.20+ if using the provided build
integration.platforms: CI covers Ubuntu 24.04 (GCC/Clang), Windows 2022 (MSVC), macOS 15 (Apple Clang); no vector intrinsics used (SWAR is plain uint64_t arithmetic), so it should build anywhere a 64-bit integer type exists
integration.thread_safety: not documented; the view holds only an immutable pointer+length with no internal mutable state, so concurrent reads of the same view look safe by inspection, but the project does not state this
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: API names and shape closely mirror std::string_view and it implicitly converts to/from std::string and std::string_view, but size_type/npos is `unsigned int` rather than std::size_t, so code comparing against std::string_view::npos or relying on 64-bit indices needs changes

gotchas: size_type and npos are `unsigned int` (32-bit), not std::size_t like std::string_view — a real interop gap, not just a naming difference
The SWAR fast path only activates when sizeof(CharT)==1 and outside constexpr evaluation; wide-char types and constexpr calls silently use the scalar loop instead
find_first_not_of and find_last_not_of are slower than std::string_view (20-26% per the README), the opposite of the library's headline claim
No LICENSE file and no license field in vcpkg.json, so legal usability is unresolved even though the source is public
pick_this_over_siblings_when: It's the only catalogued entry benchmarked against std::string_view itself (the other siblings target std::string/std::to_string), so pick it specifically when your bottleneck is string_view::find-family calls on a C++11 toolchain; for std::string construction/formatting/conversion speedups, use FastString, to_static_string, or Str instead.
verified_claims_summary: README's first-party Google Benchmark table (one ~95-char haystack, compiler/flags/stdlib unstated, hardware reported only as '12x 2096 MHz CPU') shows zuu::string_view beating std::string_view on find_first_of (6.11 vs 15.7 ns, ~2.5x), find/substring (11.1 vs 14.1 ns), rfind/substring (11.4 vs 16.7 ns), find_last_of (11.0 vs 14.7 ns), and find/char (1.56 vs 2.24 ns), while std::string_view wins on find_first_not_of (5.01 vs 6.22 ns) and find_last_not_of (5.00 vs 6.82 ns).
